title: The Reflexion-Core: the determination cannot reach outside
research_question: Can the determination (adhyavasāya) establish an external object, or is the self-experience self-luminous and self-contained?

thesis.text: The determination cannot establish anything outside: the self-experience (vimarśa) is self-luminous, un-divided from memory-cognition, and all cognition is its own shining.

rival_readings.reading: The determination establishes a real external object (the Buddhist fallback)
The 'external' is merely the strength of the practice-impression, not a thing established
Establishing is in the self; experience is self-luminous, not a thing that reaches a thing

cruxes.question: Can an inert thing (the determination's object-form) establish anything, or does establishment require the self-luminous non-inert?

open_questions: Is the 'external' appearance merely a drawing-by-impression, or does it have independent standing in any part of the cognition?
Does the reflexion-core's 'one, self-luminous, all' commit to the universal-Self (V2C), or only to per-act self-luminosity?
